newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: PALM OIL - Asia markets seen mixed, await key data.
newsitem.headline: PALM OIL - Asia markets seen mixed, await key data.

text.p: Southeast Asian palm oil markets are likely to be mixed this week with slow demand seen subduing the Indonesian market, regional traders said.
Prices in Singapore and Malaysia however, will remain firm with an expected further squeeze in the spot futures contract and nearby contract months seen boosting sentiment, they said.

Indonesian traders said the market usually slows down at the beginning of the Moslem Ramadan fasting month, but should return to normal after a few days and be active several days before the Eid al-Fitr religious holiday.
"Demand would be slow as most people will be fasting. Bulog market operation is likely to continue, but the impacts are seen as minimal," one trader in Indonesia said.
Ramadan, which began recently, will end with the Eid al-Fitr holiday celebrations on February 9 and 10 in Indonesia.
Indonesian palm olein finished last week unchanged at 1,450-55 rupiah/kg in Jakarta.
Traders in Singapore and Malaysia predicted that Malaysia's benchmark, third month position March futures contract is likely to crack the key 1,300 ringgit a tonne barrier this week.
The March futures contract closed on Friday at 1,272 ringgit a tonne. But Singapore traders said a push towards 1,300 ringgit is likely to trigger selling.

"I have a feeling we'll break through the magical 1,300 ringgit barrier," the general manager of a Singapore-based palm oil trading firm said. "If it breaks a mental barrier like 1,300, you're going to see a lot of profit-taking."

Another dealer with a European commodity house said: "The underlying tone will be firm. In the short-term, it can hold above 1,300 (ringgit). But historically, it's difficult to sustain it above that level."

Traders in Kuala Lumpur said the recent squeeze in nearby contracts, which was mainly due to lower output and good exports, will be maintained this week. "The squeeze in the February contract should continue," one dealer said.
Private Malaysian crop forecaster Ivan Wong said last week he estimated output in December to have fallen by 17.4 percent to 630,000 tonnes. He put exports in December at 660,000 tonnes.
Wong is due to release his final crop estimates for December on Tuesday before the announcement of official Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority data on January 15.
Several traders in Singapore said healthy exports will probably boost sentiment for palm oil.
(with contributions from K.T. Arasu in Jakarta and Rene Pastor in Singapore)
